children.translated_text: First Chapter
What is the cause? Is it <s>Brahman</s>? Whence are we born?
By what do we live? And where are we established?
Governed by whom, in pleasure and other conditions,
do we exist? O knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, [tell us] the law [that governs this].
Time, inherent nature, necessity, chance,
the elements, a womb, <s>Puruṣa</s> (the cosmic person) — these are to be considered [as the cause].
But it is not a combination of these, because of the existence of the self;
for the self too is powerless with respect to the cause of pleasure and pain.
Those who followed <s>dhyāna-yoga</s> (meditation) perceived
the self-power of God (<s>devātmaśakti</s>), hidden by its own qualities (<s>guṇas</s>);
He who governs all those causes,
conjoined with time and the self — He alone [rules].
Him [they perceived as] having one rim, threefold, with sixteen ends,
fifty spokes, with twenty counter-spokes,
with six sets of eight, whose one bond is of universal form,
having three paths, and one delusion arising from two causes.
[We understand it as] a river with five streams, five fierce source-mouths,
waves of the five <s>prāṇas</s> (vital breaths), whose root is the fivefold <s>buddhi</s> (intellect),
with five whirlpools, the rush of five floods of suffering,
with fifty divisions and five branches — this we contemplate.
In this great [wheel] which is the life and abode of all,
the <s>haṃsa</s> (individual soul) wanders about in the wheel of <s>Brahman</s>.
Thinking the self and the Mover to be different,
when blessed by Him, it then attains immortality.
This is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, which is sung [in the <s>Udgītha</s>];
in it is the triad, the self-established, and the imperishable.
The knowers of <s>Brahman</s>, having known the difference therein,
merged in <s>Brahman</s>, devoted to That, are freed from the womb [of rebirth].
The Lord sustains this universe, which is a combination of the perishable and the imperishable,
the manifest and the unmanifest.
The self, being without lordship, is bound because of [its identification with] the condition of being an enjoyer;
but knowing God, one is freed from all bonds.

children.text: jñājñau dvāv ajāv īśanīśāv ajā hy
children.translated_text: Two are the unborn — the knowing and the unknowing, the Lord and the non-lord; and one is the unborn [<s>Prakṛti</s>],
connected with the enjoyer and the objects of enjoyment.
And the infinite self, of universal form, is indeed a non-doer;
when one discovers this triad, that is <s>Brahman</s>.
The perishable is <s>Pradhāna</s> (primordial matter); the immortal and imperishable is <s>Hara</s> (the Destroyer).
The one God rules over both the perishable and the self.
By meditating on Him, by union with Him, and by entering into His reality,
there is finally the cessation of all <s>māyā</s> (cosmic illusion).
By knowing God, there is the falling away of all bonds;
with afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>) destroyed, [there is] the cessation of birth and death.
By meditating on Him, at the third [state], at the dissolution of the body,
there is universal sovereignty; alone, with desires fulfilled.
This is to be known as eternally dwelling in the self;
indeed, there is nothing higher to be known than this.
Knowing the enjoyer, the enjoyed, and the Mover,
all this has been declared: this is the threefold <s>Brahman</s>.
Just as the form of fire, when latent in its source,
is not visible, yet its subtle mark (<s>liṅga</s>) is not destroyed —
it can be seized again by means of the kindling-stick as its source —
so both [states] are indeed [reached] in the body by means of <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ).
Making one's own body the lower kindling-stick,
and <s>Praṇava</s> (Oṃ) the upper kindling-stick,
by the repeated practice of the churning of meditation,
one may see God as the hidden [fire].
As oil in sesame seeds, as butter in curds,
as water in river-beds, and as fire in kindling-sticks,
so the self is grasped within the self
by one who perceives it through truthfulness and <s>tapas</s> (austerity).
The all-pervading self,
like butter hidden in milk,
rooted in self-knowledge and <s>tapas</s> (austerity) —
that is <s>Brahman</s>, the highest teaching of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>; that is <s>Brahman</s>, the highest teaching of the <s>Upaniṣad</s>.
Second Chapter
<s>Savitṛ</s> (the Sun God), first yoking the mind
to truth, [directing] thoughts,
discerning the light of <s>Agni</s> (fire),
brought [it] forth from the earth.
With yoked mind, we [are ready]
for the impulse of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>,
with the power to attain heaven.
Having yoked the gods with the mind,
who go with thought to heaven, to the light,
who will produce the great radiance —
<s>Savitṛ</s> impels them forth.
They yoke the mind and they yoke their thoughts,
the sages, of the great wise sage.

children.text: vi hotrā dadhe vayunāvid eka in
children.translated_text: He alone who knows the laws has ordained the priestly functions;
great is the praise of the divine <s>Savitṛ</s>.
I yoke your ancient <s>Brahman</s> with salutations;
may my verse go forth like the sun on its path.
All the sons of the immortal listen —
they who have occupied heavenly abodes.
Where <s>Agni</s> (fire) is kindled by friction,
where <s>Vāyu</s> (wind) is controlled,
where <s>Soma</s> overflows —
there the mind is born [pure].
Through the impulse of <s>Savitṛ</s>,
one should delight in the ancient <s>Brahman</s>.
If you make your source there,
your past merit will not be destroyed.
Holding the body steady with the three [upper parts] erect,
drawing the senses into the heart with the mind,
the wise one should cross over, with the boat of <s>Brahman</s>,
all the currents that bring fear.
Having compressed the <s>prāṇas</s> (breaths) here, with controlled movements,
when the breath is diminished, one should breathe out through the nostrils.
Like a chariot yoked with vicious horses,
the wise one should restrain the mind vigilantly.
On a level, clean [ground], free from gravel, fire, and sand,
free from [disturbing] sounds, water, and shelters,
pleasing to the mind but not painful to the eye,
in a sheltered spot protected from the wind — one should practice [<s>yoga</s>].
Fog, smoke, sun, fire, wind,
fireflies, lightning, crystal, and the moon —
these are the preliminary forms
that manifest <s>Brahman</s> in <s>yoga</s>.
When the fivefold quality of <s>yoga</s>, arising from earth, water, fire, air, and ether,
has been produced,

children.text: na tasya rogo na jarā na mṛtyuḥ
children.translated_text: there is no disease, no old age, no death
for one who has obtained a body made of the fire of <s>yoga</s>.
Lightness, health, freedom from craving,
clearness of complexion, pleasantness of voice,
an agreeable odor, and scanty excretions —
they say these are the first signs of the progress of <s>yoga</s>.
Just as a mirror stained by dust
shines brightly when well cleaned,
so the embodied one, having perceived the true nature of the self (<s>ātmatattva</s>),
becomes one, fulfilled, and free from sorrow.
When, by the reality of the self as by a lamp,
the disciplined one perceives here the reality of <s>Brahman</s> —
knowing God as unborn, eternal, purified of all categories of existence (<s>tattvas</s>),
one is freed from all bonds.
This God indeed pervades all quarters;

children.text: pūrvo ha jātaḥ sa u garbhe antaḥ
children.translated_text: He was born first, and He is within the womb.
He alone is born, He will be born;
He stands facing all beings, having faces in every direction.
The God who is in fire, who is in water,
who has entered the whole world,
who is in plants, who is in trees —
to that God, salutations again and again!
Third Chapter
He who alone, possessing the net [of <s>māyā</s>], rules with His ruling powers,
who rules all the worlds with His ruling powers,
who alone [is present] at the creation and dissolution —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.

children.text: eko hi rudro na dvitīyāya tasthe
children.translated_text: For <s>Rudra</s> is one alone; they do not stand for a second.
He rules these worlds with His ruling powers.
He stands facing beings, and having created all the worlds, the protector withdraws [them] at the end of time.
Having projected forth all the worlds, He [remains] their guardian.
Having eyes everywhere and faces everywhere,
arms everywhere and feet everywhere,
the one God forges [them] together with arms and wings,
generating heaven and earth.
He who is the source and origin of the gods,
the ruler of all, <s>Rudra</s>, the great seer,
who formerly gave birth to <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the Golden Embryo) —
may He endow us with auspicious intelligence!
O <s>Rudra</s>, that auspicious (<s>śivā</s>) form of yours
which is not terrible and reveals no evil,
with that most benign body,
O dweller on the mountain (<s>Giriśānta</s>), appear to us!
O dweller on the mountain, the arrow
which you hold in your hand to shoot —
make it auspicious, O protector of the mountain (<s>Giritra</s>);
do not harm any person or living being!
Higher than that is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the great,
hidden in all beings according to their forms,
the sole enveloper of the universe —
knowing that Lord (<s>Īśa</s>), [beings] become immortal.
I know this great <s>Puruṣa</s>,
of the color of the sun, beyond darkness.
Only by knowing Him does one go beyond death;
there is no other path for going [to immortality].
Than whom there is nothing higher, nothing smaller,
than whom there is nothing subtler and nothing greater;

children.text: vṛkṣa iva stabdho divi tiṣṭhaty ekas
children.translated_text: He stands alone, motionless like a tree, established in heaven —
by that <s>Puruṣa</s> is all this filled.
That which is higher than that,
which is formless, free from affliction —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal;
but the others attain only suffering.
Having the faces, heads, and necks of all beings,
dwelling in the cave [of the heart] of all beings,
He, the Lord (<s>Bhagavān</s>), is all-pervading;
therefore He is the omnipresent, auspicious <s>Śiva</s>.
Great indeed is this Lord, the <s>Puruṣa</s>,
the instigator of <s>sattva</s> (being/goodness).
This most pure attainment —
the ruler, the imperishable light.
The <s>Puruṣa</s>, the inner self (<s>antarātmā</s>), of the size of a thumb,
always seated in the heart of beings,
conceived by the heart, by thought, by the mind —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.
The <s>Puruṣa</s> has a thousand heads,
a thousand eyes, a thousand feet.
Enveloping the earth on all sides,
He extends ten fingers' breadth beyond.
<s>Puruṣa</s> alone is all this —
what has been and what will be.
He is also the lord of immortality —
that which grows beyond through food.
That which has hands and feet everywhere,
eyes, heads, and mouths everywhere,
having ears everywhere in the world —
it stands enveloping everything.
Shining with the qualities of all the senses,
yet devoid of all the senses,
the lord and ruler of all,
the refuge and the friend of all.
In the city of nine gates, the embodied one,
the <s>haṃsa</s> (swan-soul), sports outwardly —
the controller of the whole world,
of the stationary and the moving.
Without hands and feet, [yet] swift and grasping;
He sees without eyes, He hears without ears.

children.text: sa vetti vedyaṃ na ca tasyāsti vettā
children.translated_text: He knows what is to be known, yet there is no one who knows Him —
they call Him the foremost, the great <s>Puruṣa</s>.
Subtler than the subtle, greater than the great,
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is hidden in the cave [of the heart] of this living being;
one who is free from sorrow sees Him, the desireless one,
and His majesty, the Lord, through the grace of the Creator.
I know this undecaying, ancient one,
the Self of all, all-pervading by His omnipresence;
of whom the knowers of <s>Brahman</s> declare the cessation of birth —
indeed, they proclaim Him eternal.
Chapter Four
He who is one, colorless, yet by the manifold application of His power
ordains many colors for a hidden purpose,

children.text: vi caiti cānte viśvam ādau sa devaḥ
children.translated_text: and into whom all things dissolve at the end and from whom they emerge at the beginning — that God,
may He endow us with auspicious understanding.
That indeed is <s>Agni</s> (fire), that is <s>Āditya</s> (the sun),
that is <s>Vāyu</s> (wind), and that is the moon;
that indeed is the pure, that is <s>Brahman</s>,
that is the waters, that is <s>Prajāpati</s> (Lord of creatures).
You are woman, You are man,
You are the youth and also the maiden;
You, as an old man, totter along with a staff;
You, once born, become the one whose face is everywhere.
You are the dark-blue butterfly, the green parrot, the red-eyed one,
the lightning-pregnant cloud, the seasons, the oceans;
You, who are without beginning, abide through Your all-pervading nature,
from whom all the worlds are born.
The one unborn (<s>Prakṛti</s>), red, white, and black,
who produces many offspring of like form —
one unborn (<s>jīva</s>) lies with her, enjoying her;
another unborn (the liberated Self) abandons her after her enjoyments have been consumed.
Two birds, companions always united,
cling to the same tree;
of these two, one eats the sweet fruit (<s>pippala</s>),
while the other, not eating, shines forth in radiance.
On the same tree, the individual soul (<s>puruṣa</s>), sunken,
grieves in his helplessness, bewildered;
but when he sees the other, the Lord, who is worshipped,
and His greatness, he becomes free from sorrow.
In the imperishable, supreme space of the <s>Ṛc</s> (Vedic hymns),
wherein all the gods are seated —

children.text: yas tan na veda kim ṛcā kariṣyati
children.translated_text: he who does not know That, what will the <s>Ṛc</s> do for him?

children.text: ya it tad vidus ta ime samāsate
children.translated_text: But those who know That — they are the ones who sit here [in fulfillment].
The Vedic meters, the sacrifices, the rituals, the observances,

children.text: bhūtaṃ bhavyaṃ yac ca vedā vadanti
children.translated_text: the past, the future, and all that the <s>Vedas</s> declare —
from this the wielder of <s>Māyā</s> projects this entire universe,
and in it the other (<s>jīva</s>) is confined by <s>Māyā</s>.
Know <s>Māyā</s> to be <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature),
and the wielder of <s>Māyā</s> to be the great Lord (<s>Maheśvara</s>);
by the parts that constitute Him,
this entire world is pervaded.
He who alone presides over every womb,

children.text: yasminn idaṃ saṃ ca vi caiti sarvam
children.translated_text: in whom all this comes together and dissolves —
by discerning that Lord, the bestower of boons, the adorable God,
one attains this peace supreme.
He who is the origin and the source of the gods,
the ruler over all, <s>Rudra</s>, the great seer,
who beheld <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s> (the golden embryo) being born —
may He endow us with auspicious understanding.
He who is the sovereign of the gods,
in whom the worlds find their refuge,
who rules over this two-footed and four-footed creation —
to what God shall we offer our oblation?
Subtler than the subtlest, in the midst of chaos,
the creator of the universe, of manifold forms,
the one encompasser of the whole universe —
knowing <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One), one attains supreme peace.
He alone is the protector of the world in due time,
the lord of all, hidden in all beings;
in whom the Brahma-seers and the gods are united —
by knowing Him thus, one cuts asunder the bonds of death.
Like the cream that is subtler than butter,
knowing <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One) hidden in all beings,
the one encompasser of the entire universe —
knowing that God, one is released from all bonds.
This God, the maker of all things (<s>Viśvakarmā</s>), the great Self,
is ever seated in the hearts of beings;
He is framed by the heart, by insight, by the mind —

children.text: ya etad vidur amṛtās te bhavanti
children.translated_text: those who know this become immortal.

children.text: yadātamas tan na divā na rātrir
children.translated_text: When there is no darkness, there is neither day nor night,

children.text: na san na cāsac chiva eva kevalaḥ
children.translated_text: neither being nor non-being — only <s>Śiva</s> (the Auspicious One) alone;
that is the imperishable, that is the adorable light of <s>Savitṛ</s>,
and from that has issued forth the ancient wisdom.
No one has grasped Him above,
nor across, nor in the middle;
there is no likeness of Him
whose name is Great Glory.
His form does not stand within the range of vision,
no one sees Him with the eye;
those who know Him through the heart, seated in the heart, through the mind —
they who know thus become immortal.
"He is unborn" — with this thought, a certain one,
fearful, approaches Him in surrender;
O <s>Rudra</s>, that which is Your auspicious (southern) face —
by that, protect me always.

children.text: mā nas toke tanaye mā na āyuṣi
children.translated_text: Harm us not in our children, nor in our descendants, nor in our lives,

children.text: mā no goṣu mā no aśveṣu rīriṣaḥ
children.translated_text: nor in our cattle, nor in our horses;

children.text: vīrān mā no rudra bhāmito vadhīr
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, slay not our heroes in Your anger —
with oblations we invoke You always.
Chapter Five
Two things — <s>Vidyā</s> (knowledge) and <s>Avidyā</s> (ignorance) — are hidden
in the supreme, infinite <s>Brahman</s>, concealed therein;

children.text: kṣaraṃ tv avidyā hy amṛtaṃ tu vidyā
children.translated_text: perishable is <s>Avidyā</s>, but immortal is <s>Vidyā</s> —
He who rules over both <s>Vidyā</s> and <s>Avidyā</s> is yet another.
He who alone presides over every womb,
over all forms and all sources —

children.text: ṛṣiṃ prasūtaṃ kapilaṃ yas tam agre
children.translated_text: the seer, the first-born <s>Kapila</s>, whom He
nourished with knowledge at the beginning, and whom He may be seen producing.
Spreading out each net in manifold ways,
this God gathers it back in this field;
having created again, the Lord, the sovereign,
the great Self, exercises lordship over all.

children.text: sarvā diśa ūrdhvam adhaś ca tiryak
children.translated_text: As the sun shines, illuminating
all directions — above, below, and across —
so does that one adorable, glorious God
alone preside over all that issues from its own nature.
He who is the source of the universe, who ripens what is of its own nature,
and who transforms all that is to be ripened,
He alone rules over this entire universe,
and assigns all the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).
That which is hidden in the secret of the <s>Vedas</s>, namely the <s>Upaniṣads</s>,
<s>Brahmā</s> knows that as the source of <s>Brahman</s>;

children.text: ye pūrvaṃ devā ṛṣayaś ca tad vidus
children.translated_text: the gods and seers of old who knew That —
they, filled with That, became immortal indeed.
He who possesses the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), the doer of actions that bear fruit,
the enjoyer of whatever he has done —
he, of universal form, possessing three <s>guṇas</s> and three paths,
the lord of <s>Prāṇa</s> (life-breath), wanders according to his own actions.
Of the size of a thumb, like the sun in appearance,
endowed with will and ego-sense,
with the quality of intellect and the quality of the Self —
he is seen as even smaller than the tip of a goad.
A hundredth part of the tip of a hair,
divided again a hundredfold —
such is the measure of the <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) to be known,
yet he partakes of infinity.
It (<s>jīva</s>) is neither female nor male,
nor is it neuter;
whatever body it assumes,
by that it becomes connected.
Through imagination, touch, sight, and delusion,
through the influx of food, water, and rain, the self grows and is born;
following its <s>karma</s> (actions) in due succession, the embodied one
assumes forms in various conditions.
Gross and subtle, and many in number —
the embodied one chooses forms according to its own qualities;
the cause of their connection is seen to be yet another,
through the qualities of action and the qualities of the self.
Him who is without beginning or end, in the midst of chaos,
the creator of the universe, of manifold forms,
the one encompasser of the entire universe —
knowing that God, one is released from all bonds.
Him who is to be grasped by devotion, who is called the supportless (<s>anīḍa</s>),
who causes both being and non-being, the auspicious <s>Śiva</s>,
the God who brings forth creation with its parts —
those who know Him abandon the body [and attain liberation].
Chapter Six
Some wise men speak of inherent nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) [as the cause],
others, deluded, speak of time (<s>kāla</s>);
but it is the greatness of God in the world
by which this wheel of <s>Brahman</s> is made to revolve.
By whom this entire world is always enveloped —
the knower, the author of time, possessor of <s>guṇas</s> (qualities), omniscient —
ruled by Him, this work of creation revolves,
that which is to be contemplated as earth, water, fire, wind, and space.
Having accomplished that work, He withdraws again,
having entered into union with the essence of each essence,
with one, two, three, or eight [principles],
and with time as well as the subtle qualities of the Self.
Having initiated works endowed with <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
He who assigns all existing things [to their proper places] —
in the absence of these, the destruction of accomplished works [follows];
upon the exhaustion of <s>karma</s>, he goes forth as other than the reality.
He is the beginning, the cause of union and the efficient cause;
He is seen as beyond the three divisions of time and without parts;
worship first that adorable God of universal form,
the source of all becoming, who dwells in one's own mind.
He is other and higher than the tree [of <s>saṃsāra</s>], time, and forms,
from whom this manifested world revolves;
knowing Him who brings <s>dharma</s> (righteousness), who removes sin, the lord of prosperity,
as dwelling in one's own Self — the immortal, the universal abode.
May we know Him, the supreme great Lord of all lords,
the supreme deity of all deities,
the supreme master of all masters, transcendent beyond —
the adorable God, the lord of the universe.

children.text: na tasya kāryaṃ karaṇaṃ ca vidyate
children.translated_text: No effect or instrument is found in Him,
no one is seen equal to or greater than Him;
His supreme power is heard of as manifold indeed,
and the activity of His knowledge and strength is inherent in Him.

children.text: na tasya kaścit patir asti loke
children.translated_text: No one in the world is His master,

children.text: na ceśitā naiva ca tasya liṅgaṃ
children.translated_text: nor is there any ruler over Him, nor any distinguishing mark;
He is the cause, the lord of the lords of the senses,

children.text: na cāsya kaścij janitā na cādhipaḥ
children.translated_text: and no one is His progenitor nor His lord.
Like a spider with its threads,
with threads born of <s>Pradhāna</s> (primal matter), by its own nature,
the one God covers Himself;
may He grant us absorption into <s>Brahman</s>.
The one God, hidden in all beings,
all-pervading, the inner Self of all beings,
the overseer of all actions, dwelling in all beings,
the witness, the pure consciousness, alone and beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities).
The one controller among the many who are inactive,
who makes the one seed manifold —
the wise who perceive Him as dwelling in their own Self,
to them belongs eternal bliss, and to no others.
The eternal among the eternals, the conscious among the conscious,
the one among the many, who fulfills desires —
That cause, knowable through <s>Sāṃkhya</s> (enumeration) and <s>Yoga</s> (discipline)—
knowing that God, one is freed from all bonds.

children.text: na tatra sūryo bhāti na candratārakaṃ
children.translated_text: There the sun does not shine, nor the moon and stars,
nor do these lightnings shine—how then this fire?
Everything shines only after Him who shines;
by His radiance all this is illuminated.
The one <s>Haṃsa</s> (swan, the Supreme Self) in the midst of this world,
He indeed is the fire that has entered the waters;
only by knowing Him does one pass beyond death—
there is no other path for going [to liberation].
He is the maker of the universe, the knower of all, the source of the Self,
the omniscient, the lord of time, endowed with qualities, all-knowing,
the lord of <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter) and <s>kṣetrajña</s> (the knower of the field), the ruler of the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities),
the cause of bondage, continuance, and liberation from <s>saṃsāra</s> (the cycle of rebirth).
He, being of that nature, immortal, established as the Lord,
the knower, all-pervading, the protector of this world—

children.text: sa īśe asya jagato nityam eva
children.translated_text: He rules this world eternally;
no other cause is found for His sovereignty.
He who first creates <s>Brahmā</s>

children.text: yo vai vedāṃś ca prahiṇoti tasmai
children.translated_text: and indeed delivers the <s>Vedas</s> to him—
that God, the illuminator of self-knowledge,
I, desiring liberation, truly take refuge in.
Without parts, without action, tranquil,
faultless, untainted,
the supreme bridge to immortality—
like a fire whose fuel has been consumed.
When men can roll up space
as if it were a piece of leather,
then, without knowing God,
there will be an end to suffering.
By the power of austerity and the grace of God,
<s>Śvetāśvatara</s>, the wise one, then knowing <s>Brahman</s>,
the supremely pure [teaching], to those beyond the <s>āśramas</s> (stages of life),
rightly declared [it], approved by the assembly of <s>ṛṣis</s> (seers).
The supreme secret in <s>Vedānta</s>,
declared in a former age—
it should not be given to one who is not tranquil,
nor to one who is not a son or a disciple.
He who has supreme devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to God,
and to the <s>guru</s> (teacher) as to God—
to that great soul, these matters that have been declared
shine forth, shine forth in that <s>mahātman</s> (great soul).
